issues.reason: 'Inflection only — never derivation' states that a participle used as a modifier is an adjective keeping its surface form ('a laminated worktop' -> (Member sk_worktop_1 laminated)), so 'crying children' licenses a distributed `crying` property, not a reified cry event with the group as Agent.

'The surface tense decides, mechanically', and the reified-state precedent 'Alice was ill on Friday' -> (Member sk_ill_1 ill) (Experiencer ...) (Past sk_ill_1) requires the Past atom on a state reified from a past copular clause ('the squares WERE packed').

The adjective's-PP-complement route explicitly says to 'keep the flat copular atom (dual-emit as always)', and for a definite plural that flat predication is the distributive rule over the group's members ('The trellises are wooden' -> GroupOf + the distributive rule), which the parse omits entirely.

The half that stands is the missing member-level predication (already issue 2); the half that does not is the objection to the Experiencer itself — the rule bars the flat (Member <group> <prop>), not a role atom with a group filler, and a group-level record alongside the per-member rule is exactly what the counted-plural pattern licenses.

The reviewer's own gap concedes nothing licenses an attachment for a proper-noun modifier on a common noun, and (Possession sk_group_1 reuters) is true and well-typed — Possession is opaque and 'covers ownership, kinship, and looser association alike' — so the calibration line makes it acceptable improvisation.

'Huddled in blankets' names neither a means nor a where/when/how, so the mechanical rule governs — 'the head is the preposition actually used ... in stays In' — and Instrument asserts an unstated means relation (the reviewer's premise that Instrument is limited to 'with'-phrases is itself not stated; roles are decided by the question the PP answers).
'From the cold' answers no 'whence' question, and a prepositional verb's object is specified to take the preposition-named oblique, so Source asserts an origin the text does not state.

This is the reviewer's own registered gap, not a parse defect: nothing nested inside a seal can carry a strength or confidence, so the embedded distribution rule has no way to hold its 0.9 and the parser had no alternative.

gaps_confirmed: episodic 'many houses' — 'many' is a proportion word in the generic route and is absent from the CardinalityPhrase vague-quantity lexicon, so neither route is clearly licensed
a proper-noun modifier on a common noun ('Reuters witnesses') — no attachment head is licensed
coordination inside an oblique / complement slot ('packed with crying children and the homeless') — distributive-by-default would wrongly yield two packed states
no truth value for a conjunct inside a seal — the embedded distribution rules cannot carry their own 0.9
a plural nominalized adjective as a kind ('the homeless') in GroupOf's member-kind slot
new_gaps: an adjective's PP complement over a PLURAL subject collides with the plural rule: the complement needs one state witness to hang 'with ...' on, while a copular predicate on a definite plural must distribute to the members — nothing says how the two combine (the repair keeps both, group state plus member rule)
repair_summary: Replaced the reified cry event with the distributed adjective (Implication (PartOf $y sk_children_1) (Member $y crying)); added (Past sk_packed_1) to the reified state; added the member-level distribution (Implication (PartOf $z sk_square_1) (Past (Member $z packed))) for the dual-emit flat predication, keeping the group-level Experiencer; changed (Instrument sk_huddle_1 blanket) to (In sk_huddle_1 blanket); changed (Source sk_protect_1 cold) to (From sk_protect_1 cold).
notes: Fresh variables $y / $z were used for the two added rules so they cannot unify with the existing $x inside the same sealed term. The collective one-event-many-Agents 'huddle' is licensed (an aggregate predicate like gather), so it was left alone.
